question: Parts of a tower crane and their functions?
text:
A typical **horizontal-jib tower crane** moves a load in three ways: the **hoist** raises and lowers it, the **trolley** moves it toward or away from the tower, and the **slewing unit** swings it around the tower. ([morrow.com](https://www.morrow.com/learn/tower-crane-101?utm_source=openai))

| Part | Function |
|---|---|
| **Base and foundation** | Support the crane and transfer its weight and lifting forces to the ground. |
| **Mast (tower)** | The vertical structure, usually made of stacked steel sections, that supports the upper crane and gives it height. |
| **Slewing unit (turntable)** | Uses a bearing and motor drive to rotate the upper crane around the mast. |
| **Jib (working arm)** | The long arm that gives the crane its reach and serves as a track for the trolley. |
| **Trolley** | Travels along the jib to position the hook closer to or farther from the mast. |
| **Hoist winch and wire rope** | The powered winch winds or unwinds the rope to raise or lower the hook. |
| **Hook block** | The assembly at the bottom of the hoist rope that carries the hook, where slings or other lifting gear attach. |
| **Counter-jib** | The shorter arm behind the mast that supports the counterweights and often carries machinery. |
| **Counterweights** | Heavy blocks that counteract the overturning effect of the working arm and its load. |
| **Operator’s cab and controls** | Let the operator control the crane’s movements and monitor the lift. |

These are the main parts of a typical top-slewing, horizontal-jib crane. On a **luffing-jib crane**, the arm pivots up and down to change how far the hook reaches from the tower, rather than using a trolley for that movement. ([morrow.com](https://www.morrow.com/learn/tower-crane-101?utm_source=openai))
